note.explanation: A number system uses a base to decide its place values and which digits are allowed. To convert from decimal, divide by the new base and read the remainders from bottom to top. To convert a binary number to decimal, add the place values of its 1s.
note.simple: A base tells you how many different digit values a number system uses. For example, binary uses only 0 and 1, while octal uses 0 through 7.
note.title: Numbering Systems: Bases and Conversion
steps: Identify the base you are converting from and the base you are converting to.
For decimal to binary, octal or hexadecimal, divide repeatedly by 2, 8 or 16, respectively.
Write down each remainder and continue until the quotient is 0.
Read the remainders from bottom to top.
For binary to decimal, multiply each digit by its place value and add the results.
note.answer: The number systems in this section are decimal (base 10), binary (base 2), octal (base 8), and hexadecimal (base 16).

examTips: A board question on this section may ask you to convert a number between decimal, binary, octal, and hexadecimal.
For decimal-to-base conversions, show each division, quotient, and remainder; reading the remainders from bottom to top is an important marked step.
For binary-to-octal or binary-to-hexadecimal conversions, show the groups of three or four bits and then the digit corresponding to each group.
In place-value conversions to decimal, show each digit multiplied by its power of the base, then add the terms.
Check that each digit is allowed in its number system: binary uses 0–1, octal 0–7, decimal 0–9, and hexadecimal 0–9 and A–F.

explain.title: Decimal uses base 10
explain.body: The decimal number system is a base-10 number system that consists of digit from 0 to 9 and we use it in everyday life. That's why each digit of the number represents a power of 10. In the decimal system the place values starting from the rightmost digits are 10⁰, 10¹, 10², and so on. For example, 523 = 5 × 10² + 2 × 10¹ + 3 × 10⁰ = 523.

explain.title: Binary uses base 2
explain.body: In binary, the place values are arranged from the right to left, starting with 2⁰, and ending at 2ⁿ,where each position represents a power of 2. Binary digits are 0 and 1. Computers use binary because digital circuits have two states: on and off, represented by 1 and 0.

explain.title: Octal uses base 8
explain.body: Octal is a positional numeral system with base eight, which implies that a digit to be used ranges from 0 to 7. The last digit is a single digit power of 8 while the other digits are the coefficients. In the decimal system, the place values starting from the 8⁰, 8¹, 8² and so on. Each octal digit represents three binary digits (bits) because 8 = 2³.

explain.title: Hexadecimal uses base 16
explain.body: The hexadecimal is a base 16 number system with digit number from 0 to 9 and alphabets from A to F; each digit represents 16 to the power of the position of the digit. The letter A to F stand for the numeric value of 10 to 15. Since 16 = 2⁴, each hexadecimal digit corresponds to four binary bits.

explain.title: Convert by repeated division
explain.body: To convert a decimal number to binary, octal, or hexadecimal, repeatedly divide by 2, 8, or 16 respectively. Record each remainder, continue until the quotient is 0, then read the remainders from bottom to top.

mistakes: Reading the remainders from top to bottom instead of bottom to top in decimal-to-base conversions.
Using a digit that is not allowed in the base, such as 2 in binary or 8 in octal.
For binary-to-octal or binary-to-hexadecimal conversions, grouping from the left instead of from the right.
Forgetting to add leading zeroes when a binary number needs complete groups of three or four bits.
Leaving out the place-value powers or arithmetic when converting a positional number to decimal.
